t.E949.agn: In 2025 EFSA re-evaluated oxygen and hydrogen together; stating that the two gases are of low toxicological concern as food additives and that dietary exposure is very low, it concluded that their use does not raise a safety concern. In the EU it is authorised at quantum satis (as much as needed) in all food categories, including foods for infants and young children; EFSA recommended some changes to the EU specifications.
t.E949.found.0: In the EU, may be used in many foods at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E949.found.1: As a packaging gas in packaged foods
t.E949.prod: Mostly produced chemically by reacting natural gas with steam at high temperature (steam reforming).
t.E949.regx.0: Re-evaluated together with oxygen and hydrogen; no safety concern, no ADI needed; changes to the specifications recommended.
t.E949.regx.1: Group I additive; generally authorised at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E949.summary: A gas used to replace air in packaging or as a propellant. It prevents the product from oxidising or allows it to be dispensed from spray containers.
t.E949.what: A gas used as a packaging gas.
